desc: Define the 4 diagonal direction vectors and the clockwise-turn mapping (down-right → down-left → up-left → up-right); order directions so cw(d) = (d+1)%4.

Design DP1/f tables: longest alternating run starting at (i,j) going direction d (values in {0,2}, alternating), computed via reverse-traversal; parity handled implicitly since grid value fixes the phase.
Design DP2/g tables: longest "may turn once clockwise" run: g_d[r][c] = 1 + max(straight via g_d[next], turn via f_{cw(d)}[next_cw]), terms 0 on mismatch/out-of-bounds.
Answer computation design: for each 1-cell and direction d, cand = 1 + max(g_d[next_d] if next==2, f_{cw(d)}[next_cw] if next==2); baseline 1; covers no-turn, turn-anywhere, and immediate-turn cases.
Implement the solution in the starter code (iterative DP, 8 tables, careful iteration order per direction) and validate against the 4 provided examples.
Stress-test against a brute-force walker on random small grids; verify edge cases (1x1 grid, no 1s, turn at start, zero-length second leg) and confirm O(n*m) time / acceptable memory.
